data.title: Semtech expects $480M Q4 net sales and $1.33 EPS as data center growth framework extends into fiscal 2028
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Semtech (SMTC) Q3 fiscal 2027

Management View

  • "Semtech team delivered another quarter of record financial results, driven by significant growth across our broad data center portfolio and LoRa." (President, CEO & Director Hong Hou)
  • "Third quarter revenue was a record $423 million, growing 24% sequentially and 58% year-over-year." (CEO Hou) "We delivered strong operating leverage with record adjusted earnings per share of $1.17, growing 144% year-over-year." (CEO Hou)
  • "Data center revenue was $145 million, up 45% sequentially and 158% year-over-year." (CEO Hou) "In optical, we hold significant market share in 800 gig." (CEO Hou) "We are engaged with a wide range of hyperscalers and transceiver module manufacturers on NPO, and we anticipate initial revenue in the second half of fiscal 2028." (CEO Hou)
  • "Subsequent to the Analyst Day, we achieved a new CopperEdge design win at a second leading hyperscaler, this time in a line card, our onboard application." (CEO Hou) "We expect deployment of this line card application will begin in the first half of fiscal 2028." (CEO Hou)
  • "LoRa-enabled net sales were a record $68 million, up 18% sequentially and up 69% year-over-year." (CEO Hou) "Ring launched a new line of LoRa-based sensors in the U.S. and Sidewalk is now available in Canada and Mexico with Europe, Australia and Japan expected to follow." (CEO Hou)
  • "For Q3, we recorded our 11th consecutive quarter of net sales growth with record net sales of $423 million, above the high end of the outlook range updated at our Analyst Day on October 15." (Executive VP & CFO Mark Lin) "Adjusted gross margin was 59.3%." (CFO Lin)

Outlook

  • "We expect net sales of $480 million, plus or minus $5 million." (CFO Lin) "Our outlook includes the cellular module business for the full quarter, though we continue to expect to receive regulatory clearances and close the divestiture in Q4." (CFO Lin) "A mid-quarter close would reduce cellular module revenue, but we expect it to increase adjusted operating margin with no meaningful impact on adjusted earnings per share." (CFO Lin)
  • "Our Q4 outlook now puts fiscal 2027 growth at more than 2.3x fiscal 2026." (CFO Lin) "For Q4, we expect LoRa to grow at a similar rate." (CFO Lin) "We expect high-end consumer revenue to decrease about 10% sequentially." (CFO Lin)
  • "We expect adjusted gross margin to be 58.9%, plus or minus 50 basis points." (CFO Lin) "Excluding the cellular modules business, we expect adjusted gross margin of 64.3%." (CFO Lin) "We expect gross margins to progress towards 70% in our Analyst Day model." (CFO Lin)
  • "Adjusted diluted earnings per share of $1.33, plus or minus $0.03." (CFO Lin)

Financial Results

  • "Adjusted net operating expenses were $111 million, 26% of net sales." (CFO Lin) "Our gross margin and operating expense profile flowed through to record adjusted operating income of $139 million and record adjusted operating margin of 33.0%." (CFO Lin)
  • "We also achieved record adjusted EBITDA of $146 million and record adjusted EBITDA margin of 34.5%." (CFO Lin) "Operating cash flow for Q3 was $65 million." (CFO Lin) "Free cash flow for Q3 was $55 million." (CFO Lin) "CapEx was $10 million." (CFO Lin)
  • "Our Q3 ending cash and cash equivalents balance was $251 million and principal amount of debt was $503 million, resulting in net debt of $252 million and a net leverage ratio of 0.7x, down from 1.1x at the end of Q2." (CFO Lin)

Q&A

  • Quinn Bolton, Needham & Company: "Can you give us any sense how much does that hit the top line?" (Bolton) Executive VP & CFO Lin: "On OpEx, you [ did hit it ]. We would have about 7% incremental personnel expenses, but that's embedded in our forecast."
  • Quinn Bolton, Needham & Company: "...on track to hit that sort of 50% share target in 1.6T..." (Bolton) President, CEO & Director Hou: "We're seeing the same trajectory for 1.6T TIA...we do believe we'll get to that level in the near future."
  • Timothy Arcuri, UBS: "...can that be sustained as the supply sort of normalizes out?" (Arcuri) CEO Hou: "At this point of time, the foundry capacity is not a limitation...the combination of the performance, the road map alignment and secured capacity give us the confidence for the future growth trajectory."
  • Timothy Arcuri, UBS: "...any cost like headwinds..." (Arcuri) CFO Lin: "...we're ramping the -- our photonics fab. So there's a bit of headwind there for the near term...We have NPO that's additive to our gross margin."
  • Sean O'Loughlin, TD Cowen: "...the revenue side that's contemplated in the guide for the held-for-sale modules business?" (O'Loughlin) CEO Hou: "In Q4, we're projecting a meaningful contribution of the photonics...that part of the contribution is a little bit of drag to the data center gross margin."
  • Cody Grant Acree, StoneX: "...shape of the ramp...specifically at NPO?" (Acree) CEO Hou: "...NPO...we do believe by the second half of 2027, we have a meaningful revenue contribution...we'll see the meaningful revenue in the second half of FY '28."
  • Joseph Moore, Morgan Stanley: "...potential issues with land, power..." (Moore) CEO Hou: "For networking...15% to 20% of total power consumption...linear analog solution typically save power from 90% to 50%."
  • Joseph Moore, Morgan Stanley: "...restrictions on Chinese transceiver models..." (Moore) CEO Hou: "...there would be some shift between the different customers...it wouldn't be any meaningful impact to us."
  • Richard Schafer, Oppenheimer: "...where capacity will be in units, revenues..." (Schafer) CEO Hou: "...expand the capacity by 3 to 4x by the end of this year and another 3 to 4x by the end of next year...we will be having the capacity to support a run rate of $25 million a quarter." (Schafer) Executive VP & CFO Lin: "We expect the Photonics gross margins to mirror data center gross margins."
  • Harsh Kumar, BMO: "...what are you hearing...for demand for 2028 calendar?" (Kumar) CEO Hou: "...we have the record booking in Q3 and record backlog...Our Q4 outlook now puts fiscal 2027...roughly about $520 million...we're going to be double that in FY '28 to over $1 billion."

Sentiment Analysis

  • "...gross margin is up like 30 bps...I would have thought maybe it could be up a smidge more..." (Timothy Arcuri, UBS) and "...a lot of questions on visibility" (Harsh Kumar, BMO) reflected slightly negative, detail-driven analyst tone focused on sustainability, mix, and timing.
  • "We are confident in the growth framework we outlined at our Analyst Day." (President, CEO & Director Hou) and "we believe we have a clear path to our 70% gross margin target" (Executive VP & CFO Lin) reflected positive management tone, while responses acknowledged near-term constraints with phrases such as "a bit of headwind" (CFO Lin) on photonics ramp.
  • Versus Q2, management language shifted from preparing for capacity needs ("we see the capacity we have secured may not be enough" (CEO Hou, Q2)) to emphasizing current momentum ("record booking in Q3 and record backlog" (CEO Hou, Q3)), while analyst questions broadened from capacity and product ramps (Q2) to durability into fiscal 2028 and photonics/1.6T/NPO timing (Q3).

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Q3 emphasized execution against Analyst Day ramps, with "Data center revenue was $145 million" (President, CEO & Director Hou, Q3) following Q2's "Data center revenue was a record $100 million" (CEO Hou, Q2).
  • Q3 introduced a specific second-hyperscaler CopperEdge onboard win ("a new CopperEdge design win at a second leading hyperscaler" (CEO Hou, Q3)) after Q2 described broad engagement ("engaging across a number of hyperscalers" (CEO Hou, Q2)).
  • Guidance increased from Q2’s Q3 outlook ("We currently expect net sales of $410 million" and "adjusted diluted earnings per share of $1.05" (Executive VP & CFO Lin, Q2)) to Q3’s Q4 outlook ("We expect net sales of $480 million" and "adjusted diluted earnings per share of $1.33" (CFO Lin, Q3)), alongside new disclosure on the 14-week quarter and OpEx impact.

Risks and Concerns

  • "...capacity-constrained environment" (President, CEO & Director Hou) was framed as a differentiator, and management cited mitigation as "qualified additional fabs and secure more capacity" (CEO Hou).
  • "...incremental costs as we ramp capacity of our Photonics business" (Executive VP & CFO Lin) were identified as a near-term gross margin headwind, with mitigation tied to scaling ("It really is just scaling the business" (CFO Lin)).
  • "...memory supply constraints weighing on the broader smartphone industry" (President, CEO & Director Hou) remained a consumer-market risk, partially offset by "content gains" (Executive VP & CFO Lin).

Final Takeaway

Management described Q3 as a record quarter led by data center and LoRa, and framed Q4 guidance around continued data center strength, similar sequential LoRa growth, and a seasonal consumer decline. Executives highlighted accelerating engagement across 1.6T, CopperEdge, photonics capacity expansion, and NPO timing into the second half of fiscal 2028, while acknowledging near-term photonics ramp costs and the ongoing regulatory path to closing the cellular module divestiture in Q4.

data.title: Central Garden & Pet expects FY 2027 non-GAAP EPS of $2.65 or better while forecasting Q1 loss of $0.10-$0.15
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Central Garden & Pet (CENT) Q4 fiscal 2026

Management View

  • CEO Nicholas Lahanas said fiscal 2026 reflected portfolio and operating simplification, noting, "We've exited our independent garden channel and pet distribution businesses, rationalized SKUs, moved away from lower-margin product lines and markets, consolidated businesses, and modernized our logistics network," and added, "Despite a more cautious consumer environment in both our industries, our underlying organic businesses grew, margins expanded, and earnings increased."

  • CEO Lahanas emphasized a shift from building to utilizing the network, saying, "With our modernized network now substantially complete, we're shifting from building the infrastructure to leveraging it," and tied that to customer service and e-commerce.

  • CEO Lahanas outlined M&A actions and timing, including, "At the start of fiscal year 2027, on September 30th, we completed the acquisition of Burpee, funded with cash on hand," and on TRIXIE, "We expect the transaction to close in the second quarter of fiscal 2027 and plan to fund it with cash on hand."

  • CFO Brad Smith framed the year’s reported sales decline as portfolio-driven, stating, "Net sales were $2.9 billion, down 6%, driven primarily by the exit of our pet distribution business," while adding, "Organic net sales... rose 1% overall, with 1% organic growth in both Pet and Garden."

Outlook

  • CEO Lahanas set fiscal 2027 earnings guidance and described a cautious stance: "We expect non-GAAP earnings per share of $2.65 or better," and, "we're taking a measured and cautious approach to the year ahead, recognizing the continued uncertainty in the operating environment and the pressures on consumers and our business."

  • CFO Smith detailed first-quarter expectations and key drivers: "For the first quarter, we expect a non-GAAP loss of $0.10 to $0.15 per share," adding that "a large part of the year-over-year EPS decline is driven by the inclusion of Burpee" and citing "softer consumer demand in certain pet categories" and "initial losses related to the ramp-up of our new Pet distribution partnership."

  • Compared with the prior quarter’s call, management moved from raising fiscal 2026 guidance to emphasizing fiscal 2027 pressure in Q1, with CEO Lahanas in Q3 saying, "we are raising our guidance for fiscal 2026 non-GAAP diluted EPS from $2.70 or better to $2.85 or better," versus Q4’s "$2.65 or better" outlook for fiscal 2027.

Financial Results

  • CFO Smith said fiscal 2026 profitability improved despite lower reported sales, including, "Non-GAAP operating income for the year increased 8% to $285 million," and, "We delivered record GAAP earnings per share of $3.03... and record non-GAAP earnings per share of $3.27."

  • CFO Smith described Q4 mix-driven margin expansion and a narrower loss profile, saying, "Non-GAAP gross margin expanded 480 basis points to 33.9%," and, "Non-GAAP net loss for the quarter was $2 million."

  • CFO Smith highlighted liquidity and leverage positioning for funding deals, stating, "cash and cash equivalents increased $210 million to a record high of approximately $1.1 billion," and, "Gross leverage ended the year at 2.6x... Net leverage was 0.2x."

Q&A

  • Bradley Thomas, KeyBanc Capital Markets: asked about the "puts and takes" behind the "$2.65 or higher EPS outlook"; CEO Nicholas Lahanas replied, "we are really bullish on the business and very excited," and said the pressures were "largely relegated to Q1," citing Burpee seasonality, data/AI spend, and partnership integration losses as "transitional in nature."

  • Bradley Thomas, KeyBanc Capital Markets: asked about Garden positioning, inventories, and e-commerce heading into the season; President of Garden Consumer Products Jason Barnes answered, "we had strong TDP growth in '26 of about 14%," and said for 2027 the core brands were "up another 4%," while noting "inflated inventories" in "private label fertilizers" but "outside of private label fertilizers, our inventories actually are relatively flat year-over-year."

  • Brian McNamara, Canaccord Genuity: asked to quantify Garden headwinds in Q4; CFO Brad Smith said, "If you pull out the impact of the vendor partner loss... as well as... live goods related to weather conditions, remaining sales of the Garden business were up about 2%," and CEO Nicholas Lahanas added, "it was $14 million of the $17 million that it was down."

  • Brian McNamara, Canaccord Genuity: asked where Pet consumer caution is showing; management attributed Q4 weakness to category dynamics and operational issues, including, "we had a really soft Q4 flea, fly, and tick season" and "an inventory hangover," while CEO Lahanas cited a supply disruption and said, "we've got the fill rates back up over 90%."

  • Peter Lukas (for Bob Labick), CJS Securities: asked on TRIXIE timing and earn-out mechanics; CEO Lahanas said, "they're on track to get a portion of it," and described closing as "anywhere from Jan to March" and, "on the conservative side, it may be March," while CFO Smith added the close was "most likely... toward the back half of Q2."

  • James Chartier, Monness, Crespi, Hardt & Co.: asked about organic sales expectations and fuel/oil cost impact; CFO Smith said, "we're expecting it to be flattish, so anywhere from minus 1% to plus 1% for the full year," and estimated "total cost inflation... maybe $50 million to $60 million," with CEO Lahanas adding, "Fuel being about 10% of that."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analyst sentiment was slightly negative to pressing around the step-down outlook and category softness, shown in questions such as Brian McNamara’s, "it sounds like 2027 is expected to be another challenging year," and James Chartier’s focus on what "implies EPS down" and inflation impacts.

  • Management sentiment in prepared remarks was slightly positive but cautious, with CEO Nicholas Lahanas saying, "we're taking a measured and cautious approach," while also using higher-confidence language such as "we remain confident in our long-term strategy" and "we expect... $2.65 or better."

  • Versus the prior quarter, management tone shifted from momentum and raised fiscal 2026 guidance (Q3: "We delivered another solid quarter"; "we are raising our guidance") to emphasizing near-term pressure and a Q1 loss (Q4: "we will expect Q1 to be meaningfully lower... resulting in a loss for the quarter").

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • In Q4, management expanded the acquisition narrative beyond TRIXIE with Burpee already closed, while Q3 positioned TRIXIE as the main portfolio milestone (Q3: "We entered into a definitive agreement to acquire... TRIXIE"; Q4: "we completed the acquisition of Burpee" and "expect the transaction to close in the second quarter of fiscal 2027").

  • Guidance language moved from an in-year uplift to a more conservative new-year setup, shifting from Q3’s "raising our guidance... to $2.85 or better" (fiscal 2026) to Q4’s fiscal 2027 "$2.65 or better" with an explicit Q1 loss range.

  • Analyst focus rotated from stabilization and logistics progress in Q3 toward quantifying discrete headwinds (vendor D2C shift, live goods weather, flea/fly/tick seasonality, fuel/oil inflation) and the earnings bridge behind fiscal 2027 guidance in Q4.

Risks and Concerns

  • Management cited near-term demand and retail factors, including "continued softness... in some Pet categories," "a competitive and promotional retail landscape," "select distribution losses," and "elevated retailer inventories in certain categories entering the year" (Chief Financial Officer Brad Smith).

  • Management highlighted input cost pressure and mitigation plans: CFO Smith said the company expected cost inflation and "roughly... $35 million to $40 million of pricing," and added the remainder would be addressed by "cost savings initiatives" and mix improvement.

  • Operational and integration-related risks were called out as temporary but impactful to Q1, including "a temporary supply constraint" in Pet and "initial losses" from the pet distribution partnership ramp (CFO Smith).

Final Takeaway

Management positioned fiscal 2026 as the outcome of portfolio simplification and logistics modernization, alongside record cash, while framing fiscal 2027 as a transition year with heavier commercial and data/AI investment, Burpee seasonality driving a guided Q1 loss, and TRIXIE expected to close in fiscal Q2; leadership repeatedly described several pressures as concentrated in Q1 and "transitional," while emphasizing cash-funded M&A as the top capital allocation priority and continued focus on market share, innovation, and e-commerce growth.

data.title: CrowdStrike expects $1B revenue synergies and $500M cost synergies from proposed Zscaler deal, while guiding FY 2027 net new ARR to $1.459B-$1.463B
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: CrowdStrike (CRWD) Q3 FY 2027

Management View

  • “Before I share today's exciting M&A news, I want to discuss our Q3 performance, our best quarter in company history. That makes two record quarters in a row.” (Co-Founder, President, CEO & Director George Kurtz)
  • Kurtz said Q3 included “all-time record net new ARR of $419 million,” ending ARR of “$6.26 billion,” and “revenue of $1.58 billion,” while highlighting “all-time record free cash flow of $474 million or 30% of revenue.” (CEO Kurtz)
  • Kurtz tied demand and go-to-market to AI-driven adoption, saying “Falcon Flex is the commercial harness we pioneer to drive platform consolidation and unlock rapid new product adoption,” and noted “we closed more than 1,100 net new Flex accounts… bringing total Flex accounts to more than 4,000.” (CEO Kurtz)
  • On product, Kurtz introduced agent security positioning and adoption, saying “Guardian is the fastest-growing product we've ever shipped,” and added that Guardian “following our quarter end has crossed the $100 million ARR milestone.” (CEO Kurtz)
  • Kurtz announced multiple deal actions: “we announced our intent to acquire Fiddler and Dreadnode,” and said Fiddler “brings agent observability and explainability… We'll deliver it as Falcon Observe.” (CEO Kurtz)
  • On strategy, Kurtz announced “a definitive agreement to acquire Zscaler,” framing it as end-to-end AI security: “Together, we'll secure AI on the device, in the cloud and across the network.” (CEO Kurtz)
  • “We delivered another record quarter in Q3, exceeding expectations across all guided metrics.” (Chief Financial Officer Burt Podbere)
  • Podbere emphasized breadth and operating leverage, saying “Both net and gross dollar-based retention improved for the second consecutive quarter,” and “Non-GAAP net income attributable to CrowdStrike was an all-time record $355 million or $0.34 on a diluted per share basis.” (CFO Podbere)

Outlook

  • Podbere raised full-year targets, stating “At the midpoint, we now expect approximately $1.461 billion of net new ARR for fiscal 2027,” and added “we continue to expect fiscal 2028 net new ARR growth of at least 20% year-over-year.” (CFO Podbere)
  • For Q4, Podbere guided “net new ARR of $452 million to $456 million” and revenue of “$1.638 billion to $1.644 billion,” while noting “our outlook today does not include contribution from the announced acquisition of Zscaler.” (CFO Podbere)
  • For FY 2027, Podbere guided ARR of “$6.712 billion to $6.716 billion,” total revenue of “$6.078 billion to $6.084 billion,” and non-GAAP EPS “approximately $1.28.” (CFO Podbere)
  • Compared with the prior quarter’s call, management’s FY 2027 net new ARR midpoint moved from “$1.355 billion” to “approximately $1.461 billion,” and the language remained explicit that Zscaler is excluded from current guidance. (CFO Podbere)

Financial Results

  • Podbere reported Q3 revenue of “$1.58 billion,” including subscription revenue of “$1.50 billion” and professional services revenue of “$80 million,” with revenue mix “approximately 65% from the U.S. and 35% from international geographies.” (CFO Podbere)
  • Profitability expanded as Podbere reported “Total non-GAAP gross margin was an all-time record 80%,” non-GAAP operating income of “$405 million,” and GAAP net income attributable to CrowdStrike of “$25 million.” (CFO Podbere)
  • Cash generation remained a focal point, with Podbere reporting cash and cash equivalents of “$5.37 billion,” cash flow from operations of “$665 million,” and free cash flow of “$474 million or 30% of revenue.” (CFO Podbere)

Q&A

  • Saket Kalia, Barclays: “why now? And why Zscaler?” Co-Founder, President, CEO & Director Kurtz: “we're doing it from a position of strength,” adding “Falcon Flex… is a complete unlock for customers,” and calling network security “one of the critical areas and expands our TAM to $180 billion.”
  • Brian Essex, JPMorgan: asked about “concern about vendor lock-in.” CEO Kurtz: “an open ecosystem is the ability to take data in from any other technology,” and “we have and will continue to work well with all of the other technologies in the ecosystem.” CEO Chaudhry added: “The combined solution reduces so much cost and complexity by eliminating so many network and security point products.”
  • Joseph Gallo, Jefferies: asked what ownership enables beyond “16 integrations.” CEO Kurtz: “the adversaries… is exploiting the scenes and the gaps between integrations of companies,” and said “as one platform, we can totally integrate the data sets.”
  • Brad Zelnick, Deutsche Bank: asked how “single platform, single-agent” evolves and what it means for customers using other SASE/endpoint products. CEO Kurtz: “the brand promise, single agent, that's not going to change.”
  • Meta Marshall, Morgan Stanley: asked about AI security “bottlenecks” and how the acquisition helps. CEO Kurtz: customers want to understand “shadow AI” and “secure agentic workflows,” and highlighted Zscaler’s network visibility as complementary.
  • Roger Boyd, UBS: asked why buy the category leader vs. smaller. CEO Kurtz: “Zscaler is #1.” CFO Podbere: “significantly immediately accretive to free cash flow per share before factoring any synergies.”
  • Ittai Kidron, Oppenheimer: asked to unpack “$1 billion” revenue synergies. CFO Podbere: “it will progress over the first 3 months after close,” and centered it on cross-sell plus “putting it on our platform and using Flex.”
  • Jonathan Ho, William Blair: asked about “$500 million” cost synergies and deal risks. CFO Podbere: “optimize our data center infrastructure and drive efficiencies across our vendors and broader operations.” CEO Kurtz: “you have to be maniacal about it,” while adding “we've already been working together.”

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts were slightly positive, repeatedly congratulating results and the transaction (“congrats to both the CrowdStrike and Zscaler teams… a historic combination”) while pressing on integration, lock-in risk, growth math, and synergy detail. (Saket Kalia, Barclays)
  • Management tone was positive and confident, anchored in record metrics and AI positioning; Kurtz described the deal as “a generational opportunity,” and Podbere emphasized “significantly and immediately accretive to free cash flow per share before factoring any synergies.” (CEO Kurtz; CFO Podbere)
  • Versus the prior quarter, prepared remarks expanded from “Mythos moment” demand and AIDR momentum to a transaction-led narrative centered on platform consolidation across endpoint-plus-network, with Q&A shifting heavily toward M&A rationale, integration, and synergy execution. (CEO Kurtz)

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Q3 extended the acceleration highlighted in Q2, with net new ARR rising from “$333 million” (Q2) to “$419 million” (Q3), alongside a larger focus on AI agent security (Falcon Guardian) and transaction-driven platform scope (proposed Zscaler acquisition). (CEO Kurtz)
  • Guidance language shifted from Q2’s raise to “$1.355 billion of net new ARR” midpoint to Q3’s “approximately $1.461 billion,” while maintaining the same exclusion: “Today's guidance does not include the announced Zscaler acquisition.” (CFO Podbere; CEO Kurtz)
  • Analyst focus changed from durability of “Mythos moment,” AIDR definition, token pricing, and exposure management (Q2) to deal mechanics: lock-in concerns, integration beyond partnerships, revenue/cost synergy assumptions, and combined growth profile (Q3). (Analyst Q&A)

Risks and Concerns

  • Podbere flagged timing and conditions, saying the deal is “subject to required regulatory and shareholder approvals,” and “Until closing, both companies will continue to operate independently.” (CFO Podbere)
  • On execution risk, Kurtz said, “when you do an acquisition of this scale, obviously, you've got to focus on the people, the customers the integration and you have to be maniacal about it.” (CEO Kurtz)
  • Vendor lock-in surfaced as an analyst concern; management’s mitigation message centered on interoperability, with Kurtz stating “we have and will continue to work well with all of the other technologies in the ecosystem.” (CEO Kurtz)

Final Takeaway

Management framed Q3 as a record quarter with higher FY 2027 net new ARR expectations, rapidly scaling Falcon Flex adoption, and accelerating AI agent security demand led by Falcon Guardian. Leadership positioned the proposed Zscaler acquisition—targeted to close in the second half of FY 2028—as a move to unify endpoint, cloud, and network control planes, while outlining synergy targets of approximately $1 billion in annualized run-rate revenue synergies by 30 months post-close and approximately $500 million in annualized run-rate cost synergies within 18 to 24 months.

data.title: BridgeBio gains approval of Welgemda for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy
data.description:
• The US FDA has approved BridgeBio Pharma's (BBIO) Welgemda (ribitol), the first-ever treatment for any type of limb-girdle muscular dystrophy.
  • Approval was based on data from the phase FORTIFY trial of individuals with limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9 (LGMD2I/R9). In that study, On the 100-meter timed test, a measure of ambulatory ability, patients given Welgemda showed a 0.27 m/s benefit in velocity relative to placebo at a 12-month interim analysis. Also, forced vital capacity, a measure of pulmonary function, improved approximately 3% from baseline in individuals treated with Welgemda and declined approximately 2% in the placebo cohort.
  • BridgeBio also received a Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher with the approval.
  • About 2,000 to 3,000 individuals in the US have the condition.

data.title: Local Bounti anticipates Revol Greens deal closes in days, expands footprint roughly 70% and targets ~30% higher production per square foot
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Local Bounti (LOCL) Q3 2026

Management View

  • CEO Kathleen Valiasek framed the quarter around M&A, saying, "I'm going to spend most of our time on our pending acquisition of Revol Greens' greenhouse facilities in Texas and Minnesota because I believe it is a major milestone for Local Bounti and also the industry."
  • Valiasek said the company signed a definitive deal for "2 certified-organic greenhouse facilities: a 20-acre facility in Temple, Texas; and a 10-acre facility in Medford, Minnesota, along with the Revol brand" and added, "We expect to close in the coming days."
  • On scale and positioning, Valiasek said, "Upon closing, our growing footprint will increase by roughly 70%, making Local Bounti the largest leafy greens CEA grower in the United States as measured by greenhouse acreage."
  • Valiasek emphasized near-term commercial readiness, stating, "These are operating greenhouses that are already growing product and selling to retailers under a brand that retailers and consumers in these markets already know and trust" and added, "As additional capacity at the Texas facility is sold out, we expect revenue from these facilities to grow."
  • On strategic rationale versus building, Valiasek said, "Demand for our products is outpacing our capacity" and, "Acquiring these operating facilities gets us there at a fraction of the cost and time it would take to build new capacity."
  • On product and channel expansion, Valiasek said, "because both facilities are certified organic, they will bring a new and valuable capability that will allow us to expand our assortment to meet additional customer preferences."
  • On operational upside, Valiasek stated, "we've already identified upgrades at both sites that we expect to increase production per square foot by approximately 30%" and added, "over time, we see the potential to bring our patented Stack & Flow Technology to the Texas facility."
  • Valiasek highlighted financing support and industry context, saying, "our existing strategic investor has committed to provide additional working capital in the form of a convertible note facility" and, "Capital for controlled environment agriculture is scarce."
  • CFO Anthony Hughes summarized the quarter’s industry headwinds and top line: "The Cyclospora outbreak weighed on demand for lettuce and salad products across the industry in the third quarter" and "Local Bounti sales increased 1% to $12.4 million as compared to $12.2 million in the prior year period."

Outlook

  • Management’s near-term expectation was tied to the acquisition timeline and revenue contribution: CEO Kathleen Valiasek said, "We expect to close shortly, at which point we expect the acquired facilities to begin contributing to sales in the fourth quarter," and CFO Anthony Hughes reiterated, "we expect Revol's Texas and Minnesota facilities to begin contributing to sales in the fourth quarter."
  • Hughes flagged near-term costs associated with the deal, stating, "Fourth quarter 2026 results will include transaction and integration costs related to the acquisition."
  • Relative to the prior quarter’s prepared remarks, the outlook language shifted from a general expectation—Q2: "we expect the trajectory of improvement we've demonstrated over the past several quarters to continue"—to a more event-driven focus on closing and integrating Revol Greens and adding certified-organic capacity.

Financial Results

  • CFO Anthony Hughes said demand disruption was temporary, noting, "The impact of the outbreak on our business was limited to the third quarter, and we have since seen our sales recover during the fourth quarter."
  • Hughes reported profitability metrics: "GAAP net loss for the third quarter was $17 million compared to $26.4 million in the third quarter of last year and $19.8 million in the second quarter of 2026."
  • Hughes attributed the year-over-year net loss change to operating and non-operating factors, saying, "The year-over-year improvement was primarily driven by a $3.7 million improvement in loss from operations" and "a $5.6 million favorable change in the fair value of our warrant liabilities."
  • On non-GAAP performance, Hughes said, "Adjusted EBITDA loss for the third quarter was $6.2 million compared to a loss of $7.2 million in the third quarter of last year."
  • On year-to-date trends, Hughes stated, "revenue is up 10% to $39.6 million, and adjusted EBITDA loss has improved approximately 21% to $17.8 million compared to $22.5 million in the first 9 months of last year."
  • On liquidity, Hughes said, "we ended the quarter with cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash of $11.9 million, up from $10.1 million at the end of the second quarter," and he added, "the third quarter results and the September 30 balance sheet do not include the Revol assets or the related financing."
  • On acquisition consideration and funding, Hughes stated, "We expect the acquisition to be funded primarily with secured notes through a combination of seller financing, assumed debt and new financing from our existing strategic investor for total consideration of approximately $19.6 million."

Q&A

  • No analyst Q&A session was included in this transcript.

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts: No analyst questions were included, so analyst sentiment could not be assessed from the transcript.
  • Management: Management acknowledged disruption but emphasized recovery and execution; CFO Anthony Hughes said, "we have since seen our sales recover during the fourth quarter," while CEO Kathleen Valiasek described acquisition financing in a constrained market, stating, "Capital for controlled environment agriculture is scarce."
  • Versus the prior quarter, management tone shifted from Q2’s steady-progress framing—"disciplined execution" and "trajectory"—to a more defensive explanation of category disruption and a more assertive emphasis on M&A-backed scaling.

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Strategic focus shifted from Q2’s commercial pipeline and operational efficiencies (including the single-serve salad kit "pilot launch" and network yield/cost actions) to Q3’s acquisition-led capacity expansion; CEO Kathleen Valiasek said Q3 was centered on buying capacity because "Demand for our products is outpacing our capacity" and "buying was the clear choice."
  • Guidance language evolved from Q2’s broad statement—CFO Anthony Hughes: "we expect the trajectory of improvement...to continue"—to Q3’s specific expectation tied to closing and integration: "we expect Revol's Texas and Minnesota facilities to begin contributing to sales in the fourth quarter" and "Fourth quarter 2026 results will include transaction and integration costs."
  • Reported quarterly sales were $13.9 million in Q2 (CFO Hughes) versus $12.4 million in Q3 (CFO Hughes), with Q3 explicitly linked to category weakness from Cyclospora.

Risks and Concerns

  • CEO Kathleen Valiasek described an acute industry demand shock, saying, "After the Cyclospora outbreak tied to outdoor conventional growers, many consumers just simply stopped buying lettuce and salads," while emphasizing containment: "The Cyclospora impact to Local Bounti was limited to the third quarter, and demand has since recovered."
  • Execution risk around closing and integration was explicitly acknowledged: Valiasek said, "Our focus now is on closing the transaction and preparing for integration" and Hughes said Q4 will include "transaction and integration costs."
  • Funding and industry capital availability were framed as ongoing constraints: Valiasek said, "Capital for controlled environment agriculture is scarce," and positioned the convertible note facility as incremental liquidity support.

Final Takeaway

Local Bounti’s prepared remarks centered on an expected near-term closing of the Revol Greens acquisition, which management said would expand greenhouse acreage roughly 70%, add certified-organic capabilities, and begin contributing to sales in Q4 alongside transaction and integration costs. Management attributed Q3’s softer sales level to a category-wide Cyclospora-driven demand drop that it said was limited to the quarter and has since recovered, while emphasizing improved year-over-year loss metrics, liquidity changes, and a financing structure for the deal that includes seller financing, assumed debt, and new financing from an existing strategic investor.

data.title: Tech surge sends Meta Platforms higher by 7%
data.description:
Meta Platforms (META) shares gained almost 7% on Monday. The stock finished at $597.60, up $36.76 on the day. The advance was fueled by an overall tech rally sparked by news that Jensen Huang is returning to Nvidia. The Nasdaq rose nearly 7% on Monday.

Meanwhile, Goldman Sachs named Meta among AI-related stocks that hedge funds were buying. The firm's list showed META with one of the largest increases in hedge-fund popularity during the third quarter.

Goldman also said the social platform developer added 30 hedge-fund owners in the third quarter to reach 279. That moved it from the firm's "Falling Stars" group into "Rising Stars."

Morgan Stanley analyst Brian Nowak pointed to potential catalysts, including Muse traction, AI monetization, the core advertising business and upcoming operating-expense guidance. The firm maintained its Overweight rating.
